title: Distinct agent identity
priority: Must fix before release
components: hr-helpdesk; hr postgres database; escalate_to_human; helpdesk-mcp server
problem: The agent logs in to its database with a fixed password. Escalations can also skip the gateway's identity check.
steps: 1. Do E06 first. It removes the direct route to `helpdesk-mcp` that skips the gateway. 2. Ask the platform team for short-lived database logins for role `hr_agent`. Tie them to the agent's service account. Vault dynamic roles can do this. 3. Open `k8s/deployment.yaml`. Replace the `DATABASE_URL` secret on lines 51 and 52 with the short-lived login the platform team gives you. 4. In `release/manifest.yaml` line 61, write the new login lifetime next to `database_role`. 5. Ask the platform team to show that the agent database login expires on its own. Run the E06 test to confirm no call skips the gateway.
done_when: The agent database login expires on its own, and no tool call skips the gateway.

title: All six identity fields
priority: Must fix before release
problem: Some gateway denials are logged with caller-supplied or `unknown` ids. If the denial log write fails, the failure is ignored.
steps: 1. Ask the identity team to add `agent_type_id` and `agent_instance_id` claims to the tokens the STS issues. Do not start the code steps until they confirm. 2. Open `src/gateway.py`. Replace lines 196 and 197 with `except Exception:` then `log.critical("gateway deny not audited", extra={"tool": tool})`. 3. In the same file, replace line 139 with `c.get("agent_instance_id") or "unknown",` and line 138's header lookup with `c.get("agent_type_id") or "unknown"`. 4. Ask the security team to add an alert on the log message `gateway deny not audited`. 5. Send the gateway a request with a bad token. Check that the new `audit.gateway_decisions` row has no `missing` values, or that the alert fires.
done_when: Every row in `audit.gateway_decisions` has verified type and instance ids, and a failed denial write raises an alert.

title: Trustworthy attribution
priority: Must fix before release
problem: The gateway takes the instance id from a header the caller sets. A caller can pick any id and dodge stop and rate limits.
steps: 1. Ask the identity team to add `agent_instance_id` and `agent_type_id` claims to STS tokens. Do not deploy the code steps before they confirm. 2. Open `src/credentials.py`. In the `data` dict on lines 49 to 59, add `"agent_instance_id": instance_id`. Add `instance_id` as an argument of `token()` and update its callers in `src/gateway_client.py`. 3. Open `src/gateway.py`. Replace line 170 with `instance = claims.get("agent_instance_id", "")`. 4. In the same file, add `OR (scope = 'agent_type' AND value = $4)` to the SQL on line 101, and pass `claims.get("agent_type_id")` as the fourth argument on line 102. 5. Send a call with a forged `X-Agent-Instance` header. Check that the gateway uses the id in the token, not the header.
done_when: A stop flag on an instance or agent type blocks the gateway call, even when the header says another id.
